questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The property of the alkaline earth metals that increases with their atomic number is
options: solubility of their hydroxide in water
solubility of their sulphate in water
questions.solution:
The solubility of the ionic compounds (in this case is hydroxide of alkaline earth metals ) depends on two factors, which are (i) lattice energy and (ii) hydration energy.
The lattice energy decreases more down the group as compare to the hydration energy.
Hence, solubility of alkaline earth metal increases with increase in their atomic number.
Whereas, other given properties i.e. ionisation energy, electronegativity and solubility of their sulphate in water decreases with atomic number.

questions.q:
A plot of \( \frac{1}{T} \mathrm{Vs} . \mathrm{k} \) for a reaction gives the slope \( -1 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{~K} . \) The energy of activation for the
reaction is
(Given \( R=8.314 J K^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \) )
questions.solution:
Arrhenius equation,
\( k=A e^{-\frac{E_{a}}{R T}} \rightarrow(1) \)
Taking natural log of Eq. (1), we get
\( \ln k=\ln A-\frac{E_{a}}{R} \times \frac{1}{T} \)
By plotting In \( \mathrm{k} \) against \( 1 / \mathrm{T} \), a straight line with slope \( =-\frac{E}{R} \) and intercept \( \ln \mathrm{A} \).
Now,
slope \( =-\frac{E_{a}}{R} \) \( -1 \times 10^{4}=-\frac{E_{a}}{8.314} \) \( E_{a}=8.314 \times 1 \times 10^{4} \) \( E_{a}=83.140 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify $B$ and $D$ in the following sequence of reactions.
questions.solution:
\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}_{2} \stackrel{\text { Conc. } \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\underset{(A)}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{HSO}_{4}

(addition reaction)
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{HSO}_{4} \stackrel{\Delta, \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\underset{(B)}{\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{OH}}$
(hydrolysis)

\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{OH} \stackrel{\mathrm{PBr}_{3}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CH}_{3}\underset{(c)}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{Br}

(bromination)
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{Br} \stackrel{\mathrm{Alc} . \mathrm{KOH}(\Delta)}{(\Delta)} \mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}_{2}$
(dehydrohalogenation)
Hence, $B$ and $D$ in the above given reactions are $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{CH}_{2} \mathrm{OH}$ (ethanol) and alc. $\mathrm{KOH}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For alkali metals, which one of the following trends is incorrect?
questions.solution:
In general, density increases on moving downward in a group but density of potassium (K) is lesser than that of the sodium (Na). This is because of the abnormal increase in atomic size on moving from $\mathrm{Na}(86 \mathrm{pm})$ to $\mathrm{K}(227 \mathrm{pm})$. Thus, the correct order of density is

\mathrm{Li} < \mathrm{K} < \mathrm{Na} < \mathrm{Rb}
